scope: Historical Eagle Farm compound around 1838, with the stockade, timber-slab female barracks, six-cell block, working buildings and superintendent’s and matron’s quarters.

primaryWrittenSources.facts: Captain Fyans’s March 1837 correspondence gives the single entrance, 327 by 311 feet and 17-foot height, and calls for stout poles with sharp tops.

The investigating archaeologists record double fencing, slab buildings, plaster on the supervisor’s cottage and hospital, the six-cell block and the detached kitchens. The 1842 survey and trenches tie the compound to this site. Historic ground lies below later airfield fill.
The conservation report describes the enclosure, inventories the structures in 1839 and gives written room descriptions. It identifies the farm site separately from the Brisbane Town factory.
Brisbane City Council identifies the archaeological site at 91 Schneider Road and distinguishes the extant precinct.
